caption:
This morning’s post said voice AI still breaks on the basics that block scale: context, speed, transcription and trust. I went back in and checked the numbers around that.

1.94s median reply time for GPT Realtime 2.1, versus 1.66s for Azure Realtime.
3.3% stalled-call rate for GPT Realtime 2.1, versus 2.0% for Gemini 3.8 Live.
$0.085 per minute for GPT Realtime 2.1 in Cekura’s setup, versus $0.055 for GPT-Live + Sol low.

My take: good voice is not enough. If the system is still slower, stalls more, and costs more, production will expose it fast.

Comment SDR and I will send you the details by DM.

Sources in the first comment.

scenes: This morning, the post said voice AI still breaks on context, speed, transcription and trust, so demos still do not translate into production. I went back in to check the numbers around that.
First, in Cekura’s live-call benchmark, GPT Realtime 2.1 needed 1.94 seconds median to answer, while Azure Realtime came in at 1.66.
Second, even a strong model still stalled: GPT Realtime 2.1 went silent on 3.3% of calls, versus 2.0% for Gemini 3.8 Live.
Third, cost still matters: in that benchmark setup, GPT Realtime 2.1 was priced at $0.085 per minute, versus $0.055 for GPT-Live plus Sol low.
My take: if latency, stalls and cost still move this much, the bottleneck is the system, not the voice demo.
